newsitem.title: south africa: Family says seven-year-old dead in S.African riots.
newsitem.headline: Family says seven-year-old dead in S.African riots.

text.p: A seven-year-old boy was reported shot dead in running street battles on Thursday as police fought protesters rioting over water and electricity bills in Johannesburg's mixed-race suburbs.
A visibly distraught Chantal Williams, a resident of the Eldorado Park suburb which bore much of the brunt of Thursday's violence, told national television her young brother was killed.

The residents group that organised the protest said late on Thursday, following talks with local councillors, that it had called off the action. A task team will be appointed to look into the problems.

The violence was reminiscent of street protests that marked the apartheid past but which have been rare in the country's industrial capital since Nelson Mandela became president after all-race elections in 1994.
"A white policeman and a black policeman opened fire and shot Trevor Williams, he is seven years old...Trevor Williams is dead," his sister said.

Police spokeswoman Alta Stapelberg told Reuters that officers had tried to investigate but no confirmation had been obtained: "We heard a rumour that a child was shot dead but so far nobody could confirm it."
At least 15 civilians were wounded in the clashes southwest of the city between the black township of Soweto and the city's downtown business district, police and hospital officials said.

Fourteen policemen were also hurt, most from a hail of stones and rocks, Stapelberg said. Two were in a serious condition -- one was shot in the back and the other suffered severe burns when a petrol bomb was thrown at him.
Backed by army units, police maintained a heavy presence in the affected areas on Thursday night.

Cordons were erected with razor wire, and police were still using rubber bullets and buckshot to break up stone-throwing mobs. Patrols on foot and in armoured vehicles were trying to ensure the rioters did not regroup.

Earlier stun grenades and in one case live ammunition were also used against hundreds of rioters. Tearsmoke hung heavy in the air as police tried to clear roadblocks piled with burning tyres and trash cans.
The protesters started out hurling bottles and stones but, as so often in a country awash with arms, some later resorted to gunfire.

"People have a right to peaceful protest but when others are intimidated and life and property put at risk, it is our duty to intervene," commented Superintendent Govindsamy Mariemuthoo of Soweto police.

The protests against local council threats to evict those who do not pay for the water and electricity they use were organised by the largely coloured (mixed-race) residents group, the South-Western Joint Civics Association.

Unconfirmed reports said four people were killed when police fired on protesters looting a service station. Police said they had been fired on with live ammunition and had returned fire but were unable to confirm any deaths.
